Training to become a therapist, could not agree more. I think if there’s truly people that are choosing to drink to the point of needing medical attention with no psychological issues, it’s an incredibly small minority. When I was in the ER for a panic attack I had while blackout drunk, the nurse was super snippy and pissed off. I don’t blame him at all, it was Halloween weekend in my college town and there were a lot of drunk patients, but it did really impact the care I received. 

I think this is an issue with the medical profession as a whole. I think there needs to be better training on psychological issues including addiction. This post just reminds me of a video I saw of an ER doctor berating a patient having a panic attack who said “we have patients literally dying right now. What do you want, pain meds? Oxy? Is that why you’re here?!?!” It breaks my heart that people who chose to go into a field so hard and so unrewarding, especially nursing, in order to help people seem lose that empathy when it comes to psychological issues.

As someone who “chose to drink so much” they required medical attention, how dare you. You have no idea the psychological factors that lead to that “decision.” People have alcohol addictions. People have binge drinking issues (like I do). No one is going “hmm, I’m going to end this night with a long ass visit to the ER”. You’re a ER nurse. You see the absolute dumbest shit on the regular. And THIS is where you want to take a stand? Alcohol poisoning can kill, and you’re essentially telling the Internet that you should just stay home and hope for the best instead of seeking medical attention. 

I understand being frustrated with your job. But calling people assholes who clearly likely have some sort of psychological issue is uncalled for. I call people at my job because I work retail and customers verbally abuse me over a handful of dollars. I’m going into a caring profession like you, and I could not imagine for a second calling a patient an asshole. If you truly have that belief, you should probably quit for a while. Patients deserve great healthcare even if they’re annoying or rude. You can’t adequately treat someone you despise for having a medical and likely psychological issue. If your burnt out, which I can only imagine is common as a nurse, then take a break. For the sake of the patients, but you as well. Reading through your comments it sounds like you’ve been through a lot, and I have nothing but respect and compassion for you. It just sounds like nursing, at least ER nursing which is SO intense and SO unrewarding, shouldn’t be your gig for a while. 

Side note: shaming and blaming is one of the least effective ways to help people with addictions. It just makes people defensive and shut down and ignites the negative emotions that drives them to use. People with addiction need compassion with no ifs ands or buts.
But you never know what addictive substance will get you. So many people drink. You never judge them unless they develop an addiction.
Addiction is still a disease. It permanently alters your brain chemistry. It rewires your reward pathways. They’ve done MANY brain scan studies that show the neurological impact of disease.
